# GM command reference

<!-- GENERATED by tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests/Docs (CommandReferenceRenderer) from the live command table. Do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: ARCANECORE_UPDATE_DOCS=1 dotnet test tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests --filter Docs -->

Every chat command the world daemon registers, with the account level it needs. A message that starts with `.` or `!` is a command. A command word resolves to the first table entry it is a prefix of, then the account is checked, as vmangos does; `World:GmCommands:HideUnavailable` and `ExactNameFirst` (see the [configuration reference](configuration.md)) switch to the older ArcaneCore behaviour.

Coverage: ArcaneCore implements a subset of the vmangos command table (the vmangos wiki documents several hundred commands). Commands are only listed here when they exist in this tree; there is no console command sender, so commands that vmangos allows from the server console are reachable only from an in-game account.

## Account levels

ArcaneCore stores four account levels. The vmangos levels are 0-7 (player, moderator, ticket master, game master, basic admin, developer, administrator, console), so each stored level is mapped onto a retail level by `World:GmCommands:SecurityMap`. With the default map the retail levels 2, 4 and 5 are not the level of any stored account: a command at one of them needs the next stored level above it, unless an operator remaps a stored level onto it. The **Minimum account** column below is computed from the default map.

| Stored account | Retail level (default map) | Commands reachable |
|---|---|---|
| `Player` | 0 | 6 |
| `Moderator` | 1 | 23 |
| `GameMaster` | 3 | 237 |
| `Administrator` | 6 | 347 |

The counts include the development-only commands below, which exist only when `HotReload:Commands` (for `.reload`) or the `World:HotCode` switches (for `.hotcode` and `.hotmodule`) are on; all of those default to off.

## Commands

A group (`...`) may also have a handler of its own that serves arguments naming no sub-command. **Level source** says where the level comes from: the retail table recorded in `RetailCommandLevels` (each entry cites its line of vmangos `Chat.cpp`), a level declared on the command, or the command's stored level through the map.
